screen.title: Urban Heat Islands
text: On a summer afternoon, the center of a large city can be several degrees warmer than the countryside around it. Scientists call this an urban heat island. The main cause is the material that cities are built from: asphalt, concrete and brick absorb sunlight during the day and slowly release that heat at night.

Cities also lack the natural cooling that plants provide. Trees shade the ground, and they release water vapor through their leaves, which cools the surrounding air in much the same way that sweat cools skin. Where green spaces are replaced by roads and buildings, this effect disappears.

The consequences go beyond discomfort. Warmer nights prevent people from recovering from daytime heat, and heat waves in cities are linked to more hospital visits. Some cities now paint roofs white, plant trees along streets and build parks, and early results suggest that these simple changes can lower local temperatures noticeably.

questions.stem: What is the passage mainly about?
options: The way sweat helps people stay comfortable in hot weather
The history of the building materials used in large cities
The causes and effects of extra warmth in urban areas, and possible solutions
Differences in summer weather between countries

why.en: Main idea (paraphrase). B and A mistake details (materials, sweat) for the whole.
why.tr: Ana fikir (parafraz). B ve A metindeki ayrıntıları (materials, sweat) bütün sanıyor.
why.es: Idea principal (paráfrasis). B y A confunden detalles (materiales, sudor) con el todo.

questions.stem: The word "release" in paragraph 1 is closest in meaning to
options: block
store up
reflect
give off

why.en: Vocabulary in context: release = give off.
why.es: Vocabulario en contexto: release = desprender, liberar.

questions.stem: Why does the author mention sweat in paragraph 2?
options: To compare the way trees cool the air with how sweat cools skin
To show that people in cities sweat more than people in the countryside
To suggest that hot weather is dangerous for health
To describe how plants take in water from the ground

why.en: Author's purpose: to compare how trees cool the air with a familiar process (sweating). B builds a false claim from words in the text.
why.tr: Yazarın amacı: ağaçların havayı serinletmesini tanıdık bir süreçle (terleme) karşılaştırmak. B metindeki kelimelerle yanlış bir iddia kuruyor.
why.es: Propósito del autor: comparar cómo los árboles enfrían el aire con un proceso conocido (sudar). B construye una afirmación falsa con palabras del texto.

questions.stem: What can be inferred about people who live in city centers during a heat wave?
options: They visit parks more often than other residents.
They get little relief even after the sun goes down.
They usually paint their roofs white.
They are less affected than people in the countryside.

why.en: Inference: warm nights prevent recovery. C wrongly attributes "paint roofs white" to individuals.
why.tr: Çıkarım: sıcak geceler toparlanmayı engelliyor. C metindeki "paint roofs white" ifadesini kişilere yanlış atfediyor.
why.es: Inferencia: las noches cálidas impiden la recuperación. C atribuye por error "paint roofs white" a los particulares.

questions.stem: According to paragraph 3, which step have some cities taken?
options: Opening more hospitals during heat waves
Building roads to replace green spaces
Planting trees along streets
Using darker materials on roofs

why.en: Detail: planting trees along streets. B mistakes the cause in paragraph 2 for the solution; D says the opposite.
why.tr: Detay: sokaklara ağaç dikmek. B paragraf 2'deki nedeni çözüm sanıyor; D tersini söylüyor.
why.es: Detalle: plantar árboles a lo largo de las calles. B confunde la causa del párrafo 2 con la solución; D dice lo contrario.
